newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT - Amendments to Indian Exim policy.
newsitem.headline: TEXT - Amendments to Indian Exim policy.

text.p: Following is the text of a statement by the Indian Commerce Ministry announcing changes in the Export-Import (Exim) policy:
"Ministry of Commerce has issued notification and public notice by which certain amendments have been made in the Exim Policy and Handbook (Vol. 1).

EPCG licences issued during 1992-97 Policy with 15 percent concessional rate of duty shall be entitled to import capital goods at a concessional rate of duty available in the current Exim Policy of 1997-2002. This facility shall be available only for goods yet to be cleared from customs against such licences.

The threshold limit for the purpose of recognition as Export House, Trading House, Star Trading House or Super Star Trading House has been reduced. The revised threshold limit on FOB value of exports is 25 percent higher than the threshold limit prescribed during 1996/97. The revised threshold limit on NFE value of exports is equivalent to 80 percent of the revised threshold limit on the FOB value of exports. The revised limit shall be available for one year. This has been done as per the promise made by Commerce Minister in his meeting with Export Promotion Council/Commodity Boards.

The exporters who were recognised as Export House, Trading House, Star Trading House, Super Star Trading House during 1996/97 and obtained recognition/renewal during 1997/98 have been given an option to claim SIL based upon exports made during preceding licensing year.

The items which are under Negative list of imports but are allowed under freely transferable Special Import licences can be imported by an exporter in advance and may be allowed to be cleared from customs under advance licence issued subsequently.

Under the zero duty EPCG Scheme for agricultural and allied sector, the proportion of fulfilment of export obligation over six years period has been specified. Such EPCG licence holders have to fulfil 15 percent of the export obligation in the first two years, 35 percent of the export obligation during third and fourth year and balance 50 percent of the export obligation during the fifth and sixth year of export obligation period.
DEPB rate for 1,192 items has been notified which consist of 359 Engineering items, 634 Chemicals items, 38 Textile items, 65 Electronic items, 71 Plastic items and 25 Leather products.
The deemed export benefit of refund of Terminal Excise Duty and deemed export drawback can now be availed by all exporter on monthly basis also in addition to quarterly and half yearly basis."
